A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STAR research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO, MetaWorld MT50 and real-robot experiments in Section 4, plus action-refinement ablations and learned-skill analyses in Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark success rates, real-robot trials, component ablations and codebook analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same rotation-augmented residual quantization, autoregressive causal skill transformer, action-refinement head, training objectives and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same five LIBERO suites, MetaWorld MT50 and two real-world tasks involving drawer manipulation and sequential object placement (Section 4; Appendix A).

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged in Table 1, Figure 3, Tables 3–4 and the supplementary analyses. Table 1 also retains the same externally attributed Octo and OpenVLA results. The newly cited LION and MoME works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain success-rate evaluation over 50 simulated episodes per task and 10 real-world trials, identical demonstration counts, and the same model configurations and training budgets (Section 4.1; Appendix A).

E4.justification: The rotation/autoregression ablations in Table 2, action-refinement ablation in Table 5, and codebook-utilization, dependency and quantization-loss analyses in Figures 4 and 7–9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both specify three random seeds and mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Table 1. Uncertainty reporting in the ablation tables and Figure 3 is also unchanged, with no additional statistical procedures documented.

E6.justification: All reported results, including appendix results, are retained. STAR remains at 93.6 ± 0.1 overall on LIBERO, 92.7% on MetaWorld MT50, and 3/10 drawer-task and 6/10 object-placement completions (Table 1, Figure 3, Tables 3–4).

T1.justification: The residual-quantization definitions, rotation and gradient equations, loss formulations and autoregressive factorization in Equations 1–22 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning codebook-collapse prevention, skill-dependency modeling and manipulation performance, including the abstract's approximately 12% improvement claim.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and interpretations in Section 4 and Appendices B–C are unchanged. Both retain limitations concerning manually selected codebook sizes/depths and dependence on expert-demonstration quality.

D1.justification: The first-page STAR.github.io hyperlink changes its GitHub target from JiuTian-VL/STAR to iLearn-Lab/ICML25-STAR. Appendix A's implementation, hyperparameter and hardware details remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether repository contents or availability changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Shen et al. (2024, MoME) and Chen et al. (2024a, LION) to the supervised-pretraining citations, with corresponding bibliography entries. The substantive positioning is unchanged; IGOR's change to Chen et al. (2024b) is citation disambiguation.

P1.justification: There are limited citation and punctuation edits, citation-year disambiguation, and updated first-page arXiv version/date text. The narrative, section ordering and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added references cause bibliography reflow across pages 9–11 and different line wrapping in Section 2. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–5 retain their content, captions, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds two citations and retargets the code link while preserving the scientific argument, experimental evidence, explanations and limitations, including Appendices A–C. These limited edits leave the paper's evidential strength and clarity essentially unchanged; the PDFs do not demonstrate improved code availability.
